RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-58F5CA7616-94713
Member: Cameron Alvarez, Member ID W878488198
Date of Notice: 2026-08-22
Requested Service/CPT Code: Knee arthroscopy/meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
Treating Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-18

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal Cigna's denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (arthroscopic knee meniscectomy), dated 2026-08-22, on the stated basis that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria for medical necessity." I am requesting that this decision be reversed and the procedure approved.

1. Policy Identified as Governing This Determination

Based on my own research, the medical coverage policy Cigna applies to CPT 29881 is titled, in the document itself, "CMM-312: Knee Surgery- Arthroscopic and Open Procedures," a Cigna Medical Coverage Policy developed by EviCore, with "Effective Date: August 04, 2026" — the version in effect on the date of this denial. That document's table of contents lists a dedicated section titled "Meniscectomy or Meniscal Repair," which is the subsection that contains the specific medical-necessity criteria applicable to meniscectomy procedures such as CPT 29881 (the code list in this same policy family describes CPT 29881 as "Arthroscopy, knee, surgical; with meniscectomy (medial OR lateral, including any meniscal shaving)").

I was not able to obtain or reproduce the specific bulleted/numbered medical-necessity criteria printed within that "Meniscectomy or Meniscal Repair" section. I am therefore not quoting or attributing any specific necessity criteria language to the plan in this letter beyond what is stated below, and I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Cigna/EviCore provide Cameron Alvarez and Dr. Reyes with the complete, current text of the "Meniscectomy or Meniscal Repair" criteria from CMM-312 (Effective Date: August 04, 2026) that was actually applied to reference number POC-58F5CA7616-94713, so that this appeal record can address each criterion specifically. Please treat this letter as that request.

2. Why the Clinical Record Supports Medical Necessity

Even without the benefit of the specific plan criteria language, the enclosed clinical record establishes the elements that are generally recognized — and that this plan's own policy expressly discusses — as relevant to medical necessity for meniscal surgery:

- Chronicity and severity of symptoms: Mr. Alvarez has had 24 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, with current locking, giving way, and inability to squat or kneel, limiting him to level walking only.

- Documented failed non-surgical management: CMM-312 defines "Non-Surgical Management" as follows (quoted verbatim from the policy): "any provider-directed non-surgical treatment which has been demonstrated in the scientific literature as efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of lower extremity joint pain. The types of treatment involved can include, but are not limited to, the following: relative rest/ activity modification; weight loss; supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises; prescription and non-prescription medications; assistive devices; and/or intra-articular injections." Mr. Alvarez has completed each of these modalities without durable relief:
  • Supervised physical therapy targeting quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 20 visits over 14 weeks (2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15), per the physical therapy discharge note;
  • NSAID therapy for 4 months with inadequate relief;
  • Corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-01, yielding only 4 weeks of partial relief.
  This satisfies, and in duration and modality variety exceeds, the categories of non-surgical management the plan's own policy identifies as the relevant conservative-care benchmark.

- Objective imaging confirmation of a surgical lesion: MRI of the knee dated 2026-06-23 demonstrates a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. This is not a degenerative or incidental finding but a displaced, mechanically symptomatic tear — the category of meniscal pathology most clearly amenable to arthroscopic treatment.

- Preserved joint/cartilage status: The same MRI shows articular cartilage preserved, with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes. CMM-312 itself defines Kellgren-Lawrence "Grade I" as "doubtful narrowing of joint space and possible osteophytic lipping" (quoted verbatim from the policy) — i.e., minimal osteoarthritic change. This directly rebuts any concern that the knee's symptoms are primarily attributable to advanced osteoarthritis rather than to the meniscal tear, and supports that this is an appropriate candidate for meniscal surgery rather than a knee where surgery would be excluded because of underlying degenerative joint disease.

- Correlating physical examination findings: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion, clinically corroborating the MRI-documented tear and the patient's reported mechanical locking and giving-way.

- No contraindicating comorbidities: There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI of 29, and the patient is a non-smoker — none of which would suggest a surgical contraindication.

Taken together, the record documents: (1) a specific, displaced, mechanically symptomatic meniscal tear confirmed on MRI; (2) correlating exam findings; (3) a well-preserved joint surface with only minimal (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade I) degenerative change, per the plan's own grading definition; and (4) a comprehensive, multi-modality trial of the exact categories of non-surgical management the plan's policy identifies, sustained over months, without durable benefit. This clinical picture is consistent with the type of case for which arthroscopic meniscal surgery is the standard, medically necessary next step.

3. Requested Action

I respectfully request that Cigna:
1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29881 for Mr. Alvarez; or, in the alternative,
2. Provide the specific "Meniscectomy or Meniscal Repair" criteria from CMM-312 (Effective Date: August 04, 2026) that were applied to this request, and identify precisely which criterion or criteria the reviewer found unmet, so that Dr. Reyes and I may respond to that specific point; and
3. Arrange a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Reyes and the medical director who issued this determination before the appeal decision is finalized, if that option is available under this plan.

Enclosed with this appeal are: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15, 20 visits); records of NSAID trial and the 2026-06-01 corticosteroid injection; the MRI report dated 2026-06-23; office notes documenting the physical examination findings; and a letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes. Please contact me or Dr. Reyes' office at [surgeon's office phone number] if any additional documentation is needed.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-18. I look forward to a prompt reversal of this determination.

Sincerely,

Cameron Alvarez
